title: The 100 Prisoners & 100 Boxes
prompt:
100 prisoners, 100 boxes, each box hides one prisoner's number (random order). Each prisoner may open **50 boxes** to find their own number, then all boxes are closed again. If EVERY prisoner finds their number, all go free; if even one fails, all stay. No communication after the game starts.
Random guessing gives (1/2)^100 - essentially zero. Yet a clever strategy wins ~31% of the time. What is it, and why?
hint: Each prisoner starts at the box with their own number, then follows the number they find inside.
extra: Each prisoner follows the permutation cycle starting at their own number. All succeed unless some cycle is longer than 50; a random permutation of 100 has a cycle >50 only ~69% of the time - hence ~31% success. Press Run to simulate 200 trials.

title: The Idle VM
prompt: A VM runs 24/7 at $100/month but is only used 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. You can stop it outside usage hours with zero impact. Roughly what percent of the monthly bill buys nothing?
hint: 168 hours in a week; how many are actually used?
extra: 40 of 168 weekly hours used = ~24% utilized, so ~76% of the bill pays for an idle machine.

title: Bucket of Lies
prompt: I grow when you ignore me, shrink when you review me, and I am billed by the gigabyte even when nobody reads me. What am I?
extra: Unattached (orphaned) volumes and stale object storage - the quiet line item on every cloud invoice.

title: Half Again
prompt: A project budget is approved at $1.2M. Halfway through the year you have spent $900K and the work is exactly 50% done. At this burn rate, what is the final cost?
hint: Forecast the run-rate, not the plan.
extra: $900K bought 50% of scope, so 100% costs $1.8M - a 50% overrun a rolling forecast would have caught in month 3.

title: Two Doors
prompt: One door leads to production, one to an infinite billing loop. Two guards: one always tells the truth, one always lies. You may ask ONE question to ONE guard. What do you ask?
answer: what would the other guard say|what the other guard would say|ask the other guard
hint: Make both guards point at the same door.
extra: Ask either guard which door the OTHER guard would name - both will point at the billing loop. Take the other door.
